skill.name: meeting-notes
skill.description: Turns raw meeting notes into structured minutes: conclusion first, then decisions / action items / open questions; every action item must have an owner and a deadline. Use when the user pastes meeting transcripts or rough notes and asks for minutes or a summary.
skill.summary: Create concise meeting minutes with decisions, assigned actions, deadlines, and unresolved questions.
skill.author: alapha888

content.user_title: Turn Meeting Notes into Clear Minutes
content.value_statement: Rough meeting notes can hide decisions, responsibilities, and unresolved issues. This skill organizes pasted notes into concise minutes with clear actions and explicit markers for missing details.
actual_capabilities: Open minutes with a conclusion of no more than three lines.
Separate decisions, action items, and open questions.
Phrase decisions as affirmative statements rather than discussion summaries.
List action owners and deadlines, marking missing information instead of inventing it.
Identify blockers and next steps for unresolved questions.
Check completeness and target a minutes body no longer than one-third of the source notes.
limitations: Requires user-provided notes or a transcript; it does not record or transcribe meeting audio.
Cannot verify meeting facts or recover details absent from the supplied notes.
Provides formatting instructions, not automatic task assignment, calendar scheduling, or integrations.
Output needs human review; the included example attributes an action owner more specifically than its source notes.

use_cases.title: Document project decisions
use_cases.description: Turn project discussions into concise decisions, assigned follow-up work, and unresolved dependencies.

use_cases.title: Summarize engineering meetings
use_cases.description: Separate approved technical choices from proposals, then capture implementation owners and deadlines.

use_cases.title: Prepare stakeholder minutes
use_cases.description: Organize rough stakeholder notes into readable minutes while marking missing names, dates, and next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Create basic minutes
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn these notes into meeting minutes with a short conclusion, decisions, action items, and open questions: [paste notes].
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: organize a single set of rough notes.

prompt_templates.title: Extract accountable actions
prompt_templates.prompt: Summarize these notes and list each action with its stated owner and deadline. Mark missing owners [unassigned] and missing deadlines [TBD]: [paste notes].

prompt_templates.title: Distinguish decisions from proposals
prompt_templates.prompt: Create minutes from this transcript. Separate confirmed decisions from unresolved proposals, and record stated blockers and next steps: [paste transcript].
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: summarize discussions with unresolved choices.

prompt_templates.title: Audit the minutes before delivery
prompt_templates.prompt: Produce concise minutes from these notes. Check each decision, owner, and deadline against the source; flag unsupported details and ambiguous dates: [paste notes].
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: review source accuracy before sharing minutes.

output_examples.input: The team approved a cache pilot. Maria will draft the proposal by 14 October. Pricing remains undecided until Finance shares estimates.
output: Conclusion: The team approved a cache pilot. Pricing remains unresolved.
Action: Maria will draft the proposal by 14 October.
Open question: Pricing awaits Finance estimates; follow-up owner [unassigned], deadline [TBD].

output_examples.input: Everyone agreed to test the revised onboarding checklist. Someone needs to update the guide. Launch timing was discussed but not decided.
output: Conclusion: Test the revised onboarding checklist. Launch timing remains undecided.
Decision: Test the revised onboarding checklist.
Action: Update the guide; owner [unassigned], deadline [TBD].
Open question: Launch timing; blocker [to confirm], next step [to confirm], owner [unassigned].

best_practices: Provide complete notes with explicit decisions, participant names, and dates when available.
Review every action owner and deadline against the source before sharing minutes.
Keep unresolved questions visible and confirm their blockers and next steps with attendees.
anti_patterns: Treating every proposal or discussion topic as an approved decision.
Guessing action owners, dates, or numbers that the notes do not establish.
Replaying the conversation chronologically instead of extracting conclusions.

faq.question: What input does this skill accept?
faq.answer: Paste rough meeting notes or a text transcript. The skill organizes the supplied text into structured minutes.

faq.question: What sections appear in the minutes?
faq.answer: A short conclusion comes first, followed by decisions, action items, and open questions.

faq.question: What happens when an owner or deadline is missing?
faq.answer: Missing owners receive [unassigned], and missing deadlines receive [TBD]. Other unsupported details should be marked [to confirm].

faq.question: Does it create tasks or schedule meetings?
faq.answer: No. It formats follow-up work in the minutes but includes no task-management or calendar integration.

faq.question: How long should the output be?
faq.answer: The instructions target a minutes body no longer than one-third of the raw notes, with a conclusion of at most three lines.

faq.question: Should I review the generated minutes?
faq.answer: Yes. Check decisions, owners, and dates against the notes. The included example implies an owner that its source does not explicitly assign.
